senses.def: to work together with other people or groups to achieve a shared goal
examples: The two hospitals agreed to cooperate on the new cancer study.
Local residents cooperated with police during the search.

senses.def: to be helpful by doing what someone asks you to do
examples: The suspect refused to cooperate and asked for a lawyer.
If the weather cooperates, we'll eat outside tonight.

note: Also spelled co-operate, mostly in British English. "If the weather cooperates" is a common informal expression.

senses.def: involving people or groups working together toward a shared aim
examples: The research was a cooperative effort between three universities.
The countries launched a cooperative program to clean up the river.

senses.def: willing to help and do what people ask
examples: The staff at the hotel were very cooperative when we lost our keys.
Most witnesses were cooperative, but one refused to talk.

senses.def: a business or farm owned and run by the people who work in it or use it
examples: The farmers formed a cooperative to sell their coffee directly.

note: Informally shortened to "co-op" for the noun (a food co-op, a co-op apartment).

senses.def: to organize the different parts of an activity and the people involved so that they work well together
examples: She coordinated the relief effort after the flood.
We need someone to coordinate the volunteers on race day.

senses.tr: (hareket, renk vb.) uyum sağlamak, uyumlu hale getirmek
senses.def: to make body movements work well together, or to make colors or clothes match
examples: Young children find it hard to coordinate their hand and eye movements.
She always coordinates her scarf with her shoes.

senses.def: one of a pair of numbers that show the exact position of a point on a map or graph
examples: The pilot radioed the coordinates of the crash site.

note: The verb ends in /eɪt/; the noun "coordinate" usually ends in /ət/.

senses.def: the organizing of people or groups so that they work together efficiently
examples: Better coordination between agencies could have prevented the disaster.
The event required close coordination with city officials.

senses.def: the ability to control your body so that different parts move well together
examples: Dancing is a great way to improve balance and coordination.
Too much alcohol affects your coordination.

senses.def: a person whose job is to organize an activity and the people involved in it
examples: The wedding coordinator made sure everything ran on time.
Contact the program coordinator if you have questions about the schedule.

senses.def: (informal) a police officer
examples: A cop pulled him over for running a red light.
The neighbors called the cops because the party was too loud.

note: Informal but very common in American English. "Good cop, bad cop" describes two people using friendly and tough methods together.

senses.tr: başa çıkmak, üstesinden gelmek, baş etmek
senses.def: to deal successfully with a difficult situation or problem
examples: She's coping well with the stress of her new job.
The hospital couldn't cope with the sudden rise in patients.

note: Almost always followed by "with": cope with pressure, NOT "cope pressure".

senses.def: a soft reddish-brown metal used for electrical wires, pipes, and coins
examples: Thieves stripped the copper wiring from the empty building.
Copper prices rose sharply as demand for electric cars grew.

senses.def: having a reddish-brown color like the metal
examples: She has long copper hair and green eyes.

note: In British slang, "copper" also means a police officer; Americans say "cop".

senses.def: something made to look exactly like something else, or one example of a book, newspaper, etc.
examples: Please keep a copy of the receipt for your records.
The novel sold over a million copies in its first year.

senses.def: to make something that is exactly the same as something else
examples: Copy the file onto a USB drive before you reinstall the system.
He copied the address from the envelope.

senses.def: to behave like someone else, or to cheat by using another person's work
examples: Kids often copy what they see their parents do.
The teacher caught two students copying during the exam.

senses.def: the legal right to be the only one who can publish, copy, or perform a piece of creative work
examples: The band sued the website for copyright infringement.
Who holds the copyright on these photographs?

note: Spelled with -right, not -write: it is about the right to copy.

senses.def: the most important or central part of something
examples: Trust is at the core of any good relationship.
The core of the problem is a lack of funding.

senses.def: the hard center of some fruits, or the central part of a planet
examples: He ate the apple and threw the core in the trash.
The Earth's core is extremely hot.

senses.def: most important; main or essential
examples: Honesty is one of the company's core values.
Math and reading are core subjects in every school.

note: "To the core" means completely: "She was shocked to the core."

senses.def: the place where two sides, edges, or streets meet
examples: There's a coffee shop on the corner of Main and Fifth.
Put the lamp in the corner of the room.

senses.def: a difficult situation that is hard to escape from
examples: The company has backed itself into a corner with these promises.

senses.def: to trap a person or animal so they cannot escape
examples: Reporters cornered the senator as he left the building.

note: "Cut corners" = do something cheaply or carelessly. "Around the corner" can also mean "very soon".

senses.def: connected with a large company or companies in general
examples: She left her corporate job to open a bakery.
Critics say corporate interests have too much influence on politics.

note: "Climb the corporate ladder" means to get promoted step by step inside a company.

senses.def: a large business company, especially one that is legally treated as a single unit
examples: He works for a multinational corporation with offices in 40 countries.
Large corporations often pay lower tax rates than small businesses.

senses.def: accurate or true, with no mistakes
examples: Is this the correct address for the restaurant?
You're correct: the meeting was moved to Thursday.

senses.def: right or suitable for a particular situation
examples: What's the correct way to address a judge in court?

senses.def: to make something right by fixing its mistakes, or to point out someone's mistake
examples: The teacher corrected our essays over the weekend.
Correct me if I'm wrong, but didn't you say ten o'clock?

senses.def: a change that makes something more accurate or removes a mistake
examples: The newspaper printed a correction the next day.
I made a few corrections to your report in red.

senses.def: a short drop in prices after a period of rising, especially on the stock market
examples: Analysts expect a market correction after months of rapid growth.

note: In American English, a "correctional facility" is a prison.

senses.def: in a way that is accurate or right, with no mistakes
examples: Make sure the form is filled out correctly before you submit it.
If I remember correctly, the store closes at nine.

senses.tr: ilişkili olmak, bağlantılı olmak, korelasyon göstermek
senses.def: if two things correlate, they are closely connected and one changes when the other changes
examples: Income levels correlate strongly with life expectancy.
Researchers found that screen time correlated with poor sleep in teenagers.

note: Academic word. Remember: things that correlate are not necessarily causing each other.

senses.def: a connection between two things in which one changes as the other changes
examples: There is a strong correlation between smoking and lung disease.
The study found no correlation between coffee intake and memory.

note: Common phrase: "correlation does not imply causation" (a link does not prove one thing causes the other).

senses.def: to match something or be similar or equal to it
examples: Your story doesn't correspond with what the witness said.
Each number on the map corresponds to a hiking trail.

senses.def: to exchange letters or emails with someone regularly
examples: The two scientists corresponded for years before they finally met.

senses.def: the letters or emails that someone sends and receives, or the activity of writing them
examples: The museum holds her private correspondence from the 1940s.
Please keep all correspondence with the insurance company.

senses.def: a close connection or similarity between two things
examples: There is little correspondence between what he says and what he does.

note: Uncountable when it means letters: "a lot of correspondence", not "correspondences".

senses.def: a journalist who reports on a particular subject or from a particular country
examples: She worked as a war correspondent in the Middle East for ten years.
Our White House correspondent has the latest details.

senses.tr: karşılık gelen, buna bağlı, aynı dönemdeki
senses.def: matching or connected with something just mentioned
examples: Sales rose 12% compared with the corresponding period last year.
Higher prices led to a corresponding drop in demand.

senses.def: a long narrow passage inside a building, with doors to rooms on each side
examples: His office is at the end of the corridor on the left.
Students waited in the corridor outside the exam room.

senses.def: a long strip of land or air space linking two places, often used for travel or trade
examples: The new rail line will serve the busy Boston–Washington corridor.

collocations: at the end of the corridor
note: In American homes and schools, "hallway" or "hall" is more common than "corridor".

senses.def: using power dishonestly or illegally, especially by taking money
examples: The corrupt official accepted bribes from construction firms.
Voters were tired of a corrupt system that favored the rich.

senses.def: (of computer data) damaged so that it cannot be used correctly
examples: I couldn't open the attachment because the file was corrupt.

senses.def: to make someone dishonest or immoral
examples: Power corrupts, and absolute power corrupts absolutely.

senses.def: dishonest or illegal behavior, especially by people in positions of power
examples: The mayor was arrested on corruption charges.
Corruption in the police force had become a serious problem.

senses.def: the amount of money needed to buy, make, or do something
examples: The cost of living in this city has doubled in ten years.
The company will cover the cost of your travel.

senses.def: something lost or given up in order to achieve something
examples: He finished the race, but at the cost of a serious knee injury.

senses.def: to have a particular price, or to cause the loss of something
examples: How much does it cost to fix the roof?
One careless mistake cost him his job.

note: Irregular verb: cost – cost – cost. "At all costs" means "no matter what happens".

senses.def: costing a lot of money, often more than you want to pay
examples: Replacing the old pipes will be a costly repair.
Long court cases are costly for both sides.

senses.def: causing serious problems or losses
examples: The goalkeeper's costly error gave the other team the win.

note: "Costly" is an adjective, not an adverb. Say "a costly mistake" or "it proved costly".

senses.def: clothes worn to look like someone or something else, for a party, play, or film
examples: My son wants to wear a dinosaur costume for Halloween.
The actors were still in costume after the show.

senses.def: the typical clothes of a particular country or historical period
examples: Dancers in traditional costume performed at the festival.

note: In American English a "costume party" is what the British call a "fancy-dress party". Turkish "kostüm" (suit) is "suit" in English.

senses.def: a small house, especially in the countryside or by a lake
examples: We rented a cottage by the lake for the summer.
The old stone cottage had a garden full of roses.

note: "Cottage cheese" is a soft white cheese similar to Turkish lor peyniri.

senses.def: a plant grown in warm places for the soft white fibers around its seeds
examples: The region grows cotton, wheat, and corn.
Cotton was the main crop in the American South for centuries.

senses.def: cloth or thread made from this plant
examples: I prefer cotton shirts in hot weather because they breathe.

note: A small ball of cotton for cleaning skin is a "cotton ball" in American English; "cotton wool" is British.

senses.def: used as the past form of "can" to talk about ability or permission in the past
examples: She could speak three languages by the age of ten.
We couldn't hear anything because of the noise.

senses.def: used to say that something is possible
examples: It could rain later, so take an umbrella.
That could be the reason he hasn't called.

senses.def: used to make polite requests or suggestions
examples: Could you pass me the salt, please?
You could ask your brother to help you move.

note: "Could have + past participle" = a past possibility that didn't happen: "You could have told me!" The "l" is silent.

senses.def: a group of elected people who govern a city, town, or county
examples: The city council voted to build a new public library.
She was elected to the town council last year.

senses.def: a group of people chosen to give advice, make rules, or manage an organization
examples: The UN Security Council met to discuss the crisis.
The student council organized a fundraiser for the flood victims.

note: Don't confuse with "counsel" (advice, or a lawyer), which sounds the same.

senses.def: an elected member of a city, town, or county council
examples: Local councillors met with residents to discuss the new parking rules.
She served as a councillor for twelve years before running for mayor.

note: British spelling. American English uses "councilor" or, more often, "council member" / "councilman" / "councilwoman".

senses.def: professional advice and support given to help someone deal with personal problems
examples: After the accident, he went to counselling to deal with his anxiety.
The school offers free counselling to students going through a hard time.

note: British spelling. American English spells it "counseling" (one l).

senses.def: a person trained to give advice and support to people with personal or practical problems
examples: My high school counselor helped me choose a college.
She sees a counselor once a week to talk about her divorce.

senses.def: a person who looks after children at a summer camp
examples: He worked as a camp counselor every summer during college.

note: American spelling; British is "counsellor". Don't confuse with "councilor" (council member).

senses.def: to say numbers in order, or to find the total number of things
examples: Close your eyes and count to twenty.
Election workers counted the votes late into the night.

senses.def: to be important, or to be accepted as valid
examples: Every second counts in an emergency.
The goal didn't count because he was offside.

senses.def: an act of counting, or the total number found by counting
examples: At the last count, more than 300 people had signed up.
I lost count of how many times he called.

note: "Count on someone" = rely on them: "You can always count on me."

senses.def: a long flat surface where customers are served in a shop or bank, or a work surface in a kitchen
examples: Please pay at the counter before you leave.
She left the groceries on the kitchen counter.

senses.tr: karşılık vermek, cevap vermek, karşı koymak
senses.def: to respond to criticism or an attack by arguing against it or acting against it
examples: The minister countered that the new tax would only affect the wealthy.
The company cut prices to counter the threat from cheaper rivals.

note: "Over-the-counter" medicine can be bought without a prescription. "Run counter to" means "be opposite to".

senses.def: a person or thing with the same role or function as another in a different place or situation
examples: The foreign minister met his French counterpart in Paris.
Women still earn less than their male counterparts in many industries.

senses.def: very many; too many to be counted
examples: I've told you countless times to lock the door.
The vaccine has saved countless lives.

senses.def: an area of land with its own government and borders, or the people who live there
examples: Japan is one of the safest countries in the world.
The whole country was watching the final game.

senses.def: land outside towns and cities, with fields and farms
examples: They sold their apartment and moved to the country.

senses.def: a style of popular music from the southern and western US
examples: My dad only listens to country on long road trips.

note: "The country" (with "the") often means rural areas, not the nation.

senses.def: land outside towns and cities, with fields, farms, and woods
examples: We spent the weekend biking through the Vermont countryside.
The train passed through miles of beautiful open countryside.

note: Uncountable: "the countryside", never "a countryside" or "countrysides".

senses.tr: ilçe, bölge, idari bölge (ABD'de eyaletin alt birimi)
senses.def: an area within a state or country that has its own local government
examples: Los Angeles County has more people than many US states.
The county fair is held every August.

note: In the US, a county is the level between a city and a state. Don't confuse with "country".

senses.def: a sudden, illegal, often violent seizure of power from a government
examples: The president was overthrown in a military coup.
The army attempted a coup but failed within hours.

senses.def: a surprising and impressive success
examples: Signing such a famous designer was a real coup for the small company.

note: Pronounced /kuː/: the p is silent. Short for French "coup d'état".

senses.def: two, or a small number of people or things
examples: I'll be ready in a couple of minutes.
We stayed at the beach for a couple of days.

senses.def: two people who are married or in a romantic relationship
examples: A young couple moved into the apartment next door.
They've been a couple since high school.

senses.def: to join or combine one thing with another
examples: Low wages, coupled with high rents, are pushing families out of the city.

note: In casual American speech, "a couple" often means "about two or three", not exactly two. "Coupled with" = together with.

senses.def: the ability to do something dangerous or difficult, or to face pain, without fear
examples: It took a lot of courage to speak out against her boss.
The firefighters showed great courage during the rescue.

senses.def: a series of lessons or lectures on a subject
examples: She's taking an online course in web design.
This course covers American history from 1865 to today.

senses.def: the direction something moves in, or the way a situation develops
examples: The storm changed course and headed out to sea.
The discovery changed the course of medical history.

senses.def: one part of a meal served at a time
examples: For the main course, I'll have the grilled salmon.

note: "Of course" = certainly. Also: golf course, race course. Don't confuse with "coarse" (rough), which sounds the same.

senses.def: the place where legal cases are judged, or the judge and jury who decide them
examples: The case will go to court next month.
The court ruled that the law was unconstitutional.

senses.def: an area marked for playing games like tennis or basketball
examples: The kids play basketball on the court behind the school.

senses.def: to try to win someone's support, or to act in a way that risks something bad
examples: Both candidates are courting young voters.
Driving that fast is courting disaster.

note: "Settle out of court" = reach an agreement before a judge decides.

senses.def: polite behavior that shows respect for other people
examples: He didn't even have the courtesy to call and say he'd be late.
Treat every customer with courtesy, even when they're rude.

senses.def: used to say who gave or allowed something, often for free
examples: The photos appear courtesy of the city museum.
Drinks were provided courtesy of the hotel.

note: A "courtesy car" or "courtesy shuttle" is provided free by a business.

senses.def: a child of your aunt or uncle
examples: My cousin and I grew up in the same neighborhood.
We have dozens of cousins on my mother's side.

note: English uses one word for all four Turkish relations (amca, dayı, hala, teyze çocuğu). Pronounced /ˈkʌzn/, like "buzz-n".
